questions.q: Why do income statement accounts need to reset to zero at year-end, while balance sheet accounts do not?
options: Because income statement accounts are less important than balance sheet accounts
Because income statement accounts measure performance for a specific period, and a fiscal year is the largest such period, while balance sheet accounts carry a running balance indefinitely
Because Oracle Fusion requires all expense accounts to be deleted annually
Because balance sheet accounts are recalculated every period regardless
questions.explain: Income statement accounts exist to measure a period's performance; resetting them each year lets the new year's performance be measured cleanly, while balance sheet accounts simply carry forward.

questions.q: When does the retained earnings calculation actually occur?
options: On December 31st, as a separate manual step
Only when a user runs a dedicated "Close Year" report by hand
It never happens automatically; it must always be journaled manually
Automatically, when the first period of the new fiscal year is opened
questions.explain: Retained earnings is calculated automatically as a consequence of opening the new year's first period, not as a separate manual action.

questions.q: In the LTV Manufacturing Corporation example, FY2026 net income is $412,000. What happens when January 2027 opens?
options: Retained Earnings decreases by $412,000 and expense accounts double
Nothing changes until a user manually posts a journal
The $412,000 is deleted from the ledger entirely
Retained Earnings increases by $412,000 and every revenue/expense account opens at zero
questions.explain: The net income for the closed year sweeps automatically into Retained Earnings, and income statement accounts begin the new year at zero.

questions.q: What determines which account absorbs the swept net income result each year?
options: A random account chosen by the system each year
Whichever account has the highest balance at year-end
The primary balancing segment value only
The Retained Earnings account designation configured in the chart of accounts/ledger setup
questions.explain: The retained earnings account is a configured designation (set up as part of chart of accounts/ledger configuration), which this automatic process relies on being correct.

questions.q: What is required if an adjustment to the prior fiscal year is discovered after the new year has already opened a period?
options: Nothing — retained earnings is fixed permanently once calculated
The new year must be deleted and recreated
The old year's period must be reopened, the correction posted, and retained earnings recalculates again to reflect it
The correction can simply be posted to the new year's period instead
questions.explain: Since retained earnings already swept based on the original (now incorrect) result, reopening the old period and posting the correction causes retained earnings to recalculate.
